general.title: About BIS - Bureau of Indian Standards
general.content: BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) is the National Standards Body of India, established under the BIS Act, 2016. It operates under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India. BIS is responsible for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
key_points: BIS is India's national standards body established under BIS Act, 2016
Operates under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Responsible for standardization, marking and quality certification
Headquarters located in New Delhi
Has regional offices across India
Publishes Indian Standards (IS) documents

general.title: Indian Standards (IS Documents)
general.content: An Indian Standard (IS) is a document established by consensus and approved by BIS that provides rules, guidelines or characteristics for activities or their results, aimed at the achievement of the optimum degree of order in a given context. Indian Standards are identified by IS numbers (e.g., IS 1234). They cover a wide range of sectors including machinery, chemicals, textiles, food and agriculture, electronics, and more.
key_points: Indian Standards are identified by IS numbers
Developed through consensus by technical committees
Cover sectors like machinery, chemicals, food, electronics, textiles
Available for purchase from BIS or can be viewed at BIS offices
Some standards are made mandatory through Quality Control Orders (QCOs)
Updated periodically to reflect technological advances

general.title: Quality Control Orders (QCOs)
general.content: A Quality Control Order (QCO) is a government notification issued under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, that makes BIS certification mandatory for specific products. Under a QCO, manufacturers, importers, and sellers of specified products must obtain the BIS Standard Mark before selling those products in India. QCOs are issued by various Ministries based on consumer safety, health and environment considerations.
key_points: QCOs make BIS certification mandatory for specific products
Issued by various Ministries under BIS Act, 2016
Products under QCO cannot be sold without BIS Standard Mark
Applies to manufacturers, importers, and sellers
Check the relevant Ministry website or BIS for current QCOs
Violations can result in penalties under BIS Act

certification.title: BIS Product Certification (Standard Mark)
certification.content: BIS Product Certification (also known as Standard Mark scheme) is a scheme through which BIS licenses manufacturers to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on their products after verifying that the product conforms to the relevant Indian Standard. It is a third-party certification scheme where BIS acts as the certification body.
key_points: Also called the ISI Mark scheme or Standard Mark scheme
BIS acts as third-party certification body
License allows manufacturer to use the BIS Standard Mark
Product must conform to the relevant Indian Standard
Applicable for both Indian and foreign manufacturers
License is valid for a specific period and requires renewal

certification.title: BIS Certification Process - Step by Step
certification.content: The BIS certification process involves several steps from identifying the applicable standard to receiving the license. The process is managed through BIS's online portal (Manak Online). Manufacturers need to identify the relevant Indian Standard, apply online, undergo testing and factory inspection, and receive the BIS license upon successful assessment.
key_points: Step 1: Identify the applicable Indian Standard for your product
Step 2: Check if certification is mandatory (via QCO) or voluntary
Step 3: Prepare required documents (manufacturing details, test reports, etc.)
Step 4: Apply online through BIS Manak Online portal
Step 5: Product samples are tested at BIS recognized/NABL accredited labs
Step 6: Factory inspection may be conducted by BIS officials
Step 7: BIS reviews the application and test reports
Step 8: BIS License (Standard Mark License) is granted if requirements are met

certification.title: Documents Typically Required for BIS Certification Application
certification.content: The exact documents required for BIS certification may vary depending on the product and applicable Indian Standard. The following is a general list of commonly required documents. Always verify the latest requirements from the official BIS Manak Online portal or contact BIS directly.
key_points: Application form (online via Manak Online portal)
Business registration documents (company registration, GST, etc.)
Manufacturing process details and quality control plan
Product technical specifications and drawings
Test reports from BIS recognized/NABL accredited laboratory
Factory layout and manufacturing capacity details
Declaration of conformance to the applicable Indian Standard
Additional documents as specified in the relevant IS and scheme document

certification.title: Manak Online - BIS Online Portal
certification.content: Manak Online is the official online portal of BIS through which manufacturers can apply for BIS certification, track application status, and manage their licenses. The portal is available at www.manakonline.in. It supports online submission of applications, document uploads, fee payments, and communication with BIS.
key_points: Official BIS portal for certification applications
Available at www.manakonline.in
Supports online application submission
Allows document upload and fee payment
Track application and license status
Register as a new applicant before applying

certification.title: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS)
certification.content: BIS also provides certification to foreign manufacturers whose products are imported into India. Under the Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS), foreign manufacturers can apply for BIS certification. The application is made through an authorized Indian Representative (AIR). The process includes testing at BIS recognized laboratories and factory inspection at the foreign manufacturing site.
key_points: Foreign manufacturers can get BIS certification through FMCS
Application submitted through an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR)
Product testing at BIS recognized laboratories
Factory inspection at the foreign manufacturing site by BIS
Mandatory for products under QCO being imported into India
Contact BIS or visit official website for current requirements

faqs.question: What is the ISI Mark?
faqs.answer: The ISI Mark is the Standard Mark of BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards). It is granted to products that have been certified to conform to the relevant Indian Standard. Products bearing the ISI Mark have been tested and inspected by BIS or BIS recognized laboratories. The ISI Mark is one of the most recognized product quality marks in India.

faqs.question: Is BIS certification mandatory for all products?
faqs.answer: BIS certification is not mandatory for all products. It is mandatory only for products that are notified under a Quality Control Order (QCO) issued by the Government of India. For all other products, BIS certification is voluntary. However, even for products not under a QCO, obtaining BIS certification can provide a competitive advantage and assure consumers of product quality.

faqs.question: How long does BIS certification take?
faqs.answer: The time taken for BIS certification can vary depending on the product category, complexity of the standard, and completeness of the application. Generally, the process from application to grant of license may take several weeks to months. BIS aims to process applications within defined timeframes. For the latest processing timelines, please check the BIS website or contact BIS directly.

faqs.question: What is BIS Hallmarking?
faqs.answer: BIS Hallmarking is a purity certification scheme for gold and silver jewellery in India. BIS hallmarks on gold jewellery include the BIS Mark, the fineness number (purity), the Assaying and Hallmarking Centre mark, and the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number. BIS Hallmarking is mandatory for gold jewellery sold in India as per the government notification.

faqs.question: How can I find the applicable Indian Standard for my product?
faqs.answer: To find the applicable Indian Standard for your product, you can: (1) Use the BIS website search at www.bis.gov.in to search for standards by product name or keyword, (2) Contact BIS directly or visit a BIS office, (3) Use the BIS Manak Online portal to search standards, (4) Consult with a BIS registered consultant. Note that the identification of the correct applicable standard is your responsibility, and you should verify with BIS or a qualified professional.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IS mark and ISI mark?
faqs.answer: The ISI Mark and the Standard Mark are often used interchangeably and refer to the same BIS certification mark. BIS grants the Standard Mark (which is commonly called the ISI Mark) to certified products. The term 'ISI' historically referred to 'Indian Standards Institution', the predecessor to BIS. Today, BIS is the correct name of the organization, and its mark is formally called the Standard Mark.
